domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's request for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation. References the employee, the leave type/policy, and the approving manager.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — initial state; request is being prepared by the employee, not yet visible to managers
SUBMITTED — employee has submitted the request; pending manager review
APPROVED — manager has approved the request; leave balance has been deducted
REJECTED — manager has rejected the request; rejection reason is recorded
CANCELLED — request has been withdrawn; if previously APPROVED, balance is restored

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific category of leave. Governs how many days an employee is entitled to, accrual behaviour, notice requirements, and whether manager approval is mandatory.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect and can be used for new leave requests
INACTIVE — policy has been disabled; existing balances remain but no new requests accepted under this policy
ARCHIVED — policy is retired; retained for historical reference only

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave is approved or cancelled.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is in effect; employee can draw against it
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays is zero; no further leave of this type can be taken until accrual or new fiscal year
FROZEN — balance is temporarily locked (e.g., during an audit or dispute); no deductions or accruals permitted

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organisation. Owns leave balances and submits leave requests. Has a reporting manager who approves/rejects requests.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — employee is currently employed and eligible for leave
INACTIVE — employee is on extended leave or suspension; leave accrual may be paused
TERMINATED — employment has ended; all balances are frozen and no new requests accepted

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each LeavePolicy is associated with exactly one LeaveType. The feature scope covers annual, sick, and emergency; the remaining types are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of states a LeaveRequest passes through during its lifecycle. Governs which transitions are valid and which actors may initiate them.

domain_entities.name: BalanceStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of LeaveBalance states. ACTIVE means the balance can be drawn against. EXHAUSTED means remainingDays is zero. FROZEN means the balance is temporarily locked.

domain_entities.name: EmploymentStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of employee employment states. Determines eligibility for leave requests and balance accrual.

business_rules: BR-001 — Leave request date validation: startDate must be on or before endDate. Both dates must be in the future at the time of submission (not at DRAFT time). The total requested days (inclusive of start and end) must not exceed the employee's remainingDays for the corresponding LeaveBalance.

BR-002 — Manager approval: When a LeaveRequest transitions from SUBMITTED to APPROVED, the approving manager's ID (approvedBy) must match the employee's managerId. Self-approval is prohibited — an employee cannot approve their own leave request.

BR-003 — Balance deduction on approval: When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the number of calendar days in the request range, and remainingDays is decremented accordingly. This must happen atomically — if the balance update fails, the approval must be rolled back.

BR-004 — Balance restoration on cancellation: When an APPROVED LeaveRequest transitions to CANCELLED, the previously deducted days are restored to the LeaveBalance (usedDays decremented, remainingDays incremented). Cancellation of a non-APPROVED request does not affect the balance.
BR-006 — Leave type eligibility: An employee may only submit a LeaveRequest against a LeavePolicy that is ACTIVE. If the policy is INACTIVE or ARCHIVED, the request must be rejected at submission.

BR-005 — Minimum notice period: If the LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays is set, the startDate of the LeaveRequest must be at least that many calendar days after the submission date. This rule is enforced at the point of submission (SUBMITTED transition), not at DRAFT time.

BR-007 — Employment status gate: Only employees with employmentStatus ACTIVE may submit a leave request. Employees with INACTIVE or TERMINATED status are blocked at submission. An employee whose status changes to TERMINATED while a request is SUBMITTED must have that request automatically CANCELLED.

BR-008 — Overlapping leave prevention: An employee cannot have two APPROVED or SUBMITTED LeaveRequests with overlapping date ranges for the same LeaveType. The system must check for date-range overlaps at submission time and reject if a conflict exists.

BR-009 — Fiscal year scoping: Each LeaveBalance is scoped to a single fiscalYear. When a LeaveRequest spans two fiscal years, the deduction is applied against the fiscal year in which the startDate falls. The system must not allow a request that would cause remainingDays to go negative.

BR-010 — Valid state transitions for LeaveRequest: DRAFT → SUBMITTED (by employee who owns the request); SUBMITTED → APPROVED (by manager only); SUBMITTED → REJECTED (by manager only); SUBMITTED → CANCELLED (by employee who owns the request); APPROVED → CANCELLED (by employee who owns the request, triggers balance restoration); DRAFT → CANCELLED (by employee who owns the request). Transitions not listed here are invalid and must be rejected.

BR-011 — Emergency leave bypasses minimum notice: When the LeaveType is emergency, the minimumNoticeDays constraint from LeavePolicy is not enforced. Emergency leave may be submitted with any startDate, including same-day.

BR-012 — Balance status auto-transition: When remainingDays reaches 0, the LeaveBalance status automatically transitions from ACTIVE to EXHAUSTED. When remainingDays becomes positive again (via accrual, cancellation restoration, or new fiscal year allocation), the status transitions back to ACTIVE. FROZEN is set only by an explicit administrative action and must be manually reverted.
domain_notes:
Lifecycle states introduced that must be folded into architectureMdUpdate:

**LeaveRequest** lifecycle: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED | REJECTED) → CANCELLED. CANCELLED is reachable from DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or APPROVED. APPROVED → CANCELLED triggers balance restoration.

**LeavePolicy** lifecycle: ACTIVE → INACTIVE → ARCHIVED. Only ACTIVE policies accept new leave requests.

**LeaveBalance** lifecycle: ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED (auto when remainingDays=0) → ACTIVE (auto when remainingDays>0). ACTIVE → FROZEN (admin action only, manual revert).

**Employee.employmentStatus**: ACTIVE → INACTIVE → TERMINATED. Only ACTIVE employees may submit leave requests. Termination auto-cancels any SUBMITTED requests.

**Cross-entity invariants**: LeaveRequest references Employee (via employeeId, approvedBy) and LeavePolicy (via leaveTypeId). LeaveBalance references Employee (via employeeId) and LeavePolicy (via policyId). Balance deduction/restoration is atomic with approval/cancellation transitions. Overlap detection spans LeaveRequest entities for the same employee and leave type.
